claims.text: Who filed matters here, and the driver filed. The driver's claim is a request to put a charge back — 'the $6.50 was taken back, please return my compensation'. The payments ledger shows the only line on this trip is a 6.50 SGD cancellation fee charged at 14:15:44 and reversed in full at 17:00:40 after the rider complained, leaving payment_status REFUNDED and refund_issued_sgd 6.50 (EV-FARE-05060; EV-TRIP-05060). Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative and 'never means restore a charge': the present state — rider not carrying the fee, fee withheld from the driver — is exactly what NO_ACTION preserves. The filing party's claim is a request for a charge to be reinstated, and the record contains no basis on which the rider should bear it again.

The amount the driver seeks is not the amount the policy allows, and the rider said so on the record: her statement on file reads 'I was charged $6.50 for a no-show, more than the $5 I know about'. POL-NS-26 provides that the no-show fee 'is fixed at 5.00 SGD', and POL-NS-22 states the fee the policy authorises as 5.00 SGD. This rider was charged 6.50 SGD, 1.50 SGD above the schedule, and the ledger's own computation confirms it: policy_fee_sgd 5.00 against fee_charged_sgd 6.50, with fee_matches_policy false (EV-FARE-05060; EV-TRIP-05060). POL-NS-22 itself directs that where the record charged an amount other than 5.00 SGD the ruling acts on the amount charged and adds a referral naming that clause — that check has fired on this record, and the rider should not be left carrying a charge levied outside the fixed fee. The full reversal already on the ledger is the minimum correction of that overcharge and should not be disturbed.

I do not contend the driver breached POL-NS-23, and I will not stretch the record: two in-app messages precede the cancellation (14:09:40 and 14:13:00) and one in-app call was placed at 14:12:10, unanswered, ringing 30 s, before the 14:15:40 cancellation, and the derived contact_before_cancel block marks the obligation met (EV-TRIP-05060; EV-CHAT-05060). Nor do I contend the free wait under POL-NS-21 had not run: cancellation came 385 s after the 14:09:15 arrival, past the 300 s free wait (EV-TRIP-05060). What that compliance buys the driver is the fee the schedule sets — 5.00 SGD — not the 6.50 SGD payment he asks for, and it does not cure the amount discrepancy on his own ledger.

If the judge reaches the driver-no-show test, the fact that test needs cannot be fixed on this record: the trip is on-demand, scheduled_at is null, and the derived driver_deadline block returns deadline null with the reason 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time' (EV-TRIP-05060). POL-NS-24's own note directs that where the record carries no scheduled time and the deadline cannot be fixed, POL-GEN-26 applies: the case is escalated, no monetary outcome issues and the amount is held rather than released. Escalation on that footing leaves the rider not carrying the charge, which is the only outcome consistent with a record that cannot fix the deadline the clause runs on.

The evidence package carries no traffic-data artifact for this trip at all: EV-ADVIS-05060-01 is MISSING, its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, its weight is 0.0 and it carries no payload. Under POL-GEN-02(3) a MISSING artifact carries no fact, and under POL-GEN-26 no outcome is inferred from the absence of evidence. Any suggestion that conditions on the road excused or explained how the approach and the wait were handled therefore has nothing behind it in this record, and the driver's claim cannot be strengthened by material that was never attached.

Nothing on the rider's profile can be turned against her here. Rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is 0, and even counting this trip it would be 1, below the 3 that POL-NS-25 requires before any flag; and POL-NS-25 is in any event a referral that never changes the ruling on the trip (EV-RPROF-05060). POL-GEN-01 confines profile material to the two named fields and the tests that name them, so the rider's history is not a ground for making her carry this fee — the amount question stays where the ledger puts it, at 5.00 SGD against a 6.50 SGD charge.

The free-wait test in POL-NS-21 is satisfied on this record. BECAUSE this was an on-demand trip (trip_record.scheduled_at is null), the 300 s free wait runs from the driver's arrival, and the driver marked arrived at 14:09:15 while the trip was cancelled at 14:15:40 — 385 s of waiting, which is 85 s beyond the free wait and after the record's own wait_timer_expired event at 14:14:20. The cancellation was therefore a valid rider no-show under POL-NS-21, not an early cancellation.

The driver's arrival is independently corroborated by the GPS trace, as POL-NS-21's arrival test requires. The trace has 25 fixes at a 30 s interval with 100% coverage and no gap above 30 s; the nearest fix to the pickup point is 2.893 m away at 14:09:55 with a reported accuracy of 4 m, well inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD pickup zone and inside the 25 m accuracy filter. The driver's own track then reports speed 0 from 14:09:25 through 14:15:25, showing he remained at the pickup for the entire free wait and beyond.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met on both limbs, so the FULL_REFUND trigger in that clause is not engaged. The chat log carries two in-app messages from the driver — MSG-05060-001 sent 14:09:40 and MSG-05060-002 sent 14:13:00 — and the trip record's in_app_calls list carries one in-app call placed by the driver at 14:12:10 that rang 30 s unanswered. Both limbs occurred before trip_record.cancelled_at (14:15:40), exactly as POL-NS-23 requires; a call need only be placed, and the clause says nothing about it having to be answered.

POL-NS-24 gives the rider a fee-free cancellation only where the driver fails to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes. This trip has no scheduled pickup time at all (trip_record.scheduled_at is null; the record states 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time'), so the deadline that clause needs cannot be missed, and the driver in fact arrived 6 min 20 s after acceptance and then waited. The clause's second limb — a 5.00 SGD goodwill credit — also fails, because it requires that the driver additionally failed to attempt contact, and the driver messaged and called.

No POL-GEN-26 escalation opens on this file. Every fact the operative rules need is carried by a COMPLETE artifact at weight 1.0: when the driver arrived (EV-TRIP-05060, corroborated by EV-GPS-05060), how long he waited (EV-TRIP-05060), and whether he messaged and called before cancelling (EV-CHAT-05060 and the trip record's in_app_calls). There is no open question the record cannot answer, so there is nothing for a human reviewer to resolve.

Because the wait and contact conditions are met, POL-NS-22 applies: the no-show fee is transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel, and the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION. The record charged 6.50 SGD, which is not the 5.00 SGD the clause names, and POL-NS-22's final sentence directs that where the record charged an amount other than 5.00 SGD the ruling acts on the amount charged and adds a referral naming that clause. The fare artifact's own derivation puts fee_charged_sgd and driver_compensation_if_upheld_sgd at 6.50.

NO_ACTION is not the correct outcome here and would decide the case against the driver. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION preserves the present payment state, and the present state is that the 6.50 SGD has already been refunded to the rider (payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 6.50) and withheld from the driver. The trip record shows that reversal was an interim measure taken after a rider complaint pending review, not a final determination. Leaving it standing would hand the rider a refund the policy does not give him.

The only objection the rider puts on the file is the amount — that he was charged 6.50 SGD where he knew of a 5.00 SGD fee — and he does not deny the no-show itself. That amount discrepancy is precisely what POL-NS-22's fee-amount check addresses: it produces a referral naming POL-NS-22, and POL-GEN-03 provides that such a referral does not suppress the money. It is not a ground for voiding the fee.

No confidence barrier stands in the way of a final AI ruling in the driver's favour. The dispute value is 6.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's first band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag (rider_profile.fraud_flags 0, driver_profile.fraud_flags 0), so the 0.95 confidence POL-GEN-22 requires where a party carries a fraud flag is not engaged. POL-NS-26 accordingly makes the AI ruling on this no-show final.

The no-show cancellation was valid, so the fee stands and the driver is owed his compensation (POL-NS-22); because the record charged more than the fixed 5.00 SGD fee, a referral also issues. To each of you:

Free wait (POL-NS-21). This was an on-demand trip, so the 300-second free wait ran from the driver's arrival. The driver marked arrived at 14:09:15 and cancelled at 14:15:40 — 385 seconds of waiting, past the 14:14:15 expiry and past the record's own wait_timer_expired event at 14:14:20 (EV-TRIP-05060). Arrival is corroborated as the arrival test requires: EV-GPS-05060 holds 25 fixes at 30-second intervals with no gap over 30 s and full coverage, and the nearest fix to the pickup is 2.893 m away at 14:09:55 with 4 m reported accuracy — inside the 50 m STANDARD radius and inside the 25 m accuracy filter. The driver's track then reports speed 0 from 14:09:25 to 14:15:25.

Contact (POL-NS-23). The driver sent two in-app messages (14:09:40 and 14:13:00) and placed one in-app call (14:12:10, ringing 30 s unanswered), all before the 14:15:40 cancellation (EV-CHAT-05060; EV-TRIP-05060). Both limbs are met, so no FULL_REFUND arises. The rider advocate did not contend otherwise.

Driver no-show (POL-NS-24). This clause gives the rider a fee-free cancellation only where the rider cancels because the driver did not arrive on time. The rider never cancelled — the driver did — and the driver's arrival is established on the record. The on-demand trip carries no scheduled time, so the clause's deadline cannot be fixed, but nothing turns on that gap: the clause's own trigger never occurred. POL-GEN-26 therefore does not open. Every fact the operative rules need — arrival, length of wait, whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling, and the amount charged — is carried by a complete artifact at weight 1.0. EV-ADVIS-05060-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0) and carries no fact; nothing is inferred from its absence.

Outcome (POL-NS-22 / POL-GEN-03). With the wait and contact conditions met, the fee stands and POL-NS-22 applies: the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with both money fields carrying the amount charged. The 6.50 SGD reversal on the ledger was an interim measure taken after the rider's complaint and pending review (EV-TRIP-05060, fee_reversed at 17:00:40), not a final determination. NO_ACTION is party-relative and, under POL-GEN-03, never means 'restore a charge' — it cannot give the driver the compensation he is owed, so the driver's request cannot be met by leaving the refund standing.

Amount and referral (POL-NS-22). The ledger charged 6.50 SGD, not the 5.00 SGD the policy fixes (EV-FARE-05060: fee_charged_sgd 6.50, policy_fee_sgd 5.00, fee_matches_policy false). POL-NS-22 directs that where the record charged an amount other than 5.00 SGD the ruling acts on the amount charged and adds a referral naming the clause. Both fields therefore carry 6.50 SGD and the fee-amount check is referred. The rider's point that she was charged 6.50 SGD against the 5.00 SGD she knew of is correct on the ledger and is exactly why the referral issues — but it is an amount objection, not a ground for voiding the fee, and she does not deny the no-show. Her request that the present refund simply stand is not supported.

Profile material (POL-GEN-01, POL-NS-25). Nothing on either profile decides this trip. Neither party carries a fraud flag (rider 0, driver 0), and the rider's no-show counter is 0 — even counting this trip it would be 1, below the 3 that POL-NS-25 needs before any flag. No profile history is used as a ground for the outcome.

Confidence. The deciding facts rest on artifacts all at weight 1.0 (EV-TRIP-05060, EV-GPS-05060, EV-CHAT-05060, EV-FARE-05060), so the cap is 1.0. The dispute value is 6.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's first band, and no party carries a fraud flag, so POL-NS-26 makes this ruling final at any confidence. Confidence 0.95.

ruling.explanation:
To the driver: your no-show cancellation was validly carried out, so the fee stands and the ruling goes your way. Because TRP-05060 was on-demand, POL-NS-21 runs the 300 s free wait from your arrival; you marked arrived at 14:09:15 and cancelled at 14:15:40, 385 s later, past the wait (EV-TRIP-05060, wait_timer_expired 14:14:20). The GPS trace corroborates the arrival (EV-GPS-05060): nearest fix 2.89 m from the pickup with 4 m reported accuracy, well inside the STANDARD 50 m arrival radius and the 25 m accuracy filter, and speed 0 from 14:09:25 to 14:15:25. Your POL-NS-23 contact obligation is met on both limbs — messages at 14:09:40 and 14:13:00 (EV-CHAT-05060) and a call placed at 14:12:10 (EV-TRIP-05060) — all before the 14:15:40 cancellation, so no FULL_REFUND arises. POL-NS-22 accordingly makes the ruling DRIVER_COMPENSATION. However, the ledger charged 6.50 SGD, not the 5.00 SGD the clause fixes (EV-FARE-05060: fee_charged_sgd 6.50, policy_fee_sgd 5.00, fee_matches_policy false). POL-NS-22 directs that where the record charged an amount other than 5.00 SGD the ruling acts on the amount charged and adds a referral naming that clause, so both money fields carry 6.50 SGD and the POL-NS-22 referral above accompanies the ruling; POL-GEN-03 confirms a referral never suppresses the money.

To the rider: both of your points are answered. First, POL-NS-24 cannot give you a free cancellation here and does not send this case to a human reviewer. It asks whether the driver arrived later than the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes, and this on-demand trip has no scheduled pickup time at all (trip_record.scheduled_at is null; the derived driver_deadline block returns deadline null for that reason). The test has no schedule to run against, finds nothing qualifying, and no goodwill credit follows (the driver attempted contact in any case). POL-GEN-26 does not open either: every fact the operative rules need — when the driver arrived, how long he waited, and whether he messaged and called before cancelling — is carried by COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0 (EV-TRIP-05060, EV-GPS-05060, EV-CHAT-05060), so nothing is missing or impaired. The single absent artifact, EV-ADVIS-05060-01 (MISSING, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT), is a traffic advisory that carries no fact under POL-GEN-02(3) and that no operative rule needs. Second, your point about the amount is well taken but does not void the fee: the 6.50 SGD charged exceeds the 5.00 SGD fixed fee, and that is precisely what POL-NS-22's fee-amount check addresses — it produces the referral, not a refund. NO_ACTION is rejected: the driver's claim is supported on this record, and the 17:00:40 reversal was an interim measure taken pending review, not a final determination.

On the profiles and confidence: neither profile carries a fraud flag (rider_profile.fraud_flags 0, driver_profile.fraud_flags 0), so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 requirement is not engaged; with a dispute value of 6.50 SGD this is an AI-final no-show under POL-NS-26. No POL-NS-25 flag arises: rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is not present on this record, and POL-NS-25 (C7) applies only where that counter is present. Confidence 0.9: every artifact carrying the deciding facts — EV-TRIP-05060, EV-GPS-05060, EV-CHAT-05060 and EV-FARE-05060 — is at weight 1.0, so the cap is 1.0.

ledger.claim: Who filed matters here, and the driver filed. The driver's claim is a request to put a charge back — 'the $6.50 was taken back, please return my compensation'. The payments ledger shows the only line on this trip is a 6.50 SGD cancellation fee charged at 14:15:44 and reversed in full at 17:00:40 after the rider complained, leaving payment_status REFUNDED and refund_issued_sgd 6.50 (EV-FARE-05060; EV-TRIP-05060). Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative and 'never means restore a charge': the present state — rider not carrying the fee, fee withheld from the driver — is exactly what NO_ACTION preserves. The filing party's claim is a request for a charge to be reinstated, and the record contains no basis on which the rider should bear it again.

The amount the driver seeks is not the amount the policy allows, and the rider said so on the record: her statement on file reads 'I was charged $6.50 for a no-show, more than the $5 I know about'. POL-NS-26 provides that the no-show fee 'is fixed at 5.00 SGD', and POL-NS-22 states the fee the policy authorises as 5.00 SGD. This rider was charged 6.50 SGD, 1.50 SGD above the schedule, and the ledger's own computation confirms it: policy_fee_sgd 5.00 against fee_charged_sgd 6.50, with fee_matches_policy false (EV-FARE-05060; EV-TRIP-05060). POL-NS-22 itself directs that where the record charged an amount other than 5.00 SGD the ruling acts on the amount charged and adds a referral naming that clause — that check has fired on this record, and the rider should not be left carrying a charge levied outside the fixed fee. The full reversal already on the ledger is the minimum correction of that overcharge and should not be disturbed.

I do not contend the driver breached POL-NS-23, and I will not stretch the record: two in-app messages precede the cancellation (14:09:40 and 14:13:00) and one in-app call was placed at 14:12:10, unanswered, ringing 30 s, before the 14:15:40 cancellation, and the derived contact_before_cancel block marks the obligation met (EV-TRIP-05060; EV-CHAT-05060). Nor do I contend the free wait under POL-NS-21 had not run: cancellation came 385 s after the 14:09:15 arrival, past the 300 s free wait (EV-TRIP-05060). What that compliance buys the driver is the fee the schedule sets — 5.00 SGD — not the 6.50 SGD payment he asks for, and it does not cure the amount discrepancy on his own ledger.

If the judge reaches the driver-no-show test, the fact that test needs cannot be fixed on this record: the trip is on-demand, scheduled_at is null, and the derived driver_deadline block returns deadline null with the reason 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time' (EV-TRIP-05060). POL-NS-24's own note directs that where the record carries no scheduled time and the deadline cannot be fixed, POL-GEN-26 applies: the case is escalated, no monetary outcome issues and the amount is held rather than released. Escalation on that footing leaves the rider not carrying the charge, which is the only outcome consistent with a record that cannot fix the deadline the clause runs on.

The evidence package carries no traffic-data artifact for this trip at all: EV-ADVIS-05060-01 is MISSING, its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, its weight is 0.0 and it carries no payload. Under POL-GEN-02(3) a MISSING artifact carries no fact, and under POL-GEN-26 no outcome is inferred from the absence of evidence. Any suggestion that conditions on the road excused or explained how the approach and the wait were handled therefore has nothing behind it in this record, and the driver's claim cannot be strengthened by material that was never attached.

Nothing on the rider's profile can be turned against her here. Rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is 0, and even counting this trip it would be 1, below the 3 that POL-NS-25 requires before any flag; and POL-NS-25 is in any event a referral that never changes the ruling on the trip (EV-RPROF-05060). POL-GEN-01 confines profile material to the two named fields and the tests that name them, so the rider's history is not a ground for making her carry this fee — the amount question stays where the ledger puts it, at 5.00 SGD against a 6.50 SGD charge.

The free-wait test in POL-NS-21 is satisfied on this record. BECAUSE this was an on-demand trip (trip_record.scheduled_at is null), the 300 s free wait runs from the driver's arrival, and the driver marked arrived at 14:09:15 while the trip was cancelled at 14:15:40 — 385 s of waiting, which is 85 s beyond the free wait and after the record's own wait_timer_expired event at 14:14:20. The cancellation was therefore a valid rider no-show under POL-NS-21, not an early cancellation.

The driver's arrival is independently corroborated by the GPS trace, as POL-NS-21's arrival test requires. The trace has 25 fixes at a 30 s interval with 100% coverage and no gap above 30 s; the nearest fix to the pickup point is 2.893 m away at 14:09:55 with a reported accuracy of 4 m, well inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD pickup zone and inside the 25 m accuracy filter. The driver's own track then reports speed 0 from 14:09:25 through 14:15:25, showing he remained at the pickup for the entire free wait and beyond.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met on both limbs, so the FULL_REFUND trigger in that clause is not engaged. The chat log carries two in-app messages from the driver — MSG-05060-001 sent 14:09:40 and MSG-05060-002 sent 14:13:00 — and the trip record's in_app_calls list carries one in-app call placed by the driver at 14:12:10 that rang 30 s unanswered. Both limbs occurred before trip_record.cancelled_at (14:15:40), exactly as POL-NS-23 requires; a call need only be placed, and the clause says nothing about it having to be answered.

POL-NS-24 gives the rider a fee-free cancellation only where the driver fails to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes. This trip has no scheduled pickup time at all (trip_record.scheduled_at is null; the record states 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time'), so the deadline that clause needs cannot be missed, and the driver in fact arrived 6 min 20 s after acceptance and then waited. The clause's second limb — a 5.00 SGD goodwill credit — also fails, because it requires that the driver additionally failed to attempt contact, and the driver messaged and called.

No POL-GEN-26 escalation opens on this file. Every fact the operative rules need is carried by a COMPLETE artifact at weight 1.0: when the driver arrived (EV-TRIP-05060, corroborated by EV-GPS-05060), how long he waited (EV-TRIP-05060), and whether he messaged and called before cancelling (EV-CHAT-05060 and the trip record's in_app_calls). There is no open question the record cannot answer, so there is nothing for a human reviewer to resolve.

Because the wait and contact conditions are met, POL-NS-22 applies: the no-show fee is transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel, and the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION. The record charged 6.50 SGD, which is not the 5.00 SGD the clause names, and POL-NS-22's final sentence directs that where the record charged an amount other than 5.00 SGD the ruling acts on the amount charged and adds a referral naming that clause. The fare artifact's own derivation puts fee_charged_sgd and driver_compensation_if_upheld_sgd at 6.50.

NO_ACTION is not the correct outcome here and would decide the case against the driver. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION preserves the present payment state, and the present state is that the 6.50 SGD has already been refunded to the rider (payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 6.50) and withheld from the driver. The trip record shows that reversal was an interim measure taken after a rider complaint pending review, not a final determination. Leaving it standing would hand the rider a refund the policy does not give him.

The only objection the rider puts on the file is the amount — that he was charged 6.50 SGD where he knew of a 5.00 SGD fee — and he does not deny the no-show itself. That amount discrepancy is precisely what POL-NS-22's fee-amount check addresses: it produces a referral naming POL-NS-22, and POL-GEN-03 provides that such a referral does not suppress the money. It is not a ground for voiding the fee.

No confidence barrier stands in the way of a final AI ruling in the driver's favour. The dispute value is 6.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's first band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag (rider_profile.fraud_flags 0, driver_profile.fraud_flags 0), so the 0.95 confidence POL-GEN-22 requires where a party carries a fraud flag is not engaged. POL-NS-26 accordingly makes the AI ruling on this no-show final.
